The S3 presign runner refreshes external attachment links every 12 hours. It is wired into server startup in `server/server.go` around lines 153–171 inside `startBackgroundRunners`.

The S3 presign runner (`s3presign.Runner` in `server/runner/s3presign`) refreshes external attachment links every 12 hours.

It is wired into server startup at `server/server.go:129` inside `Server.Start`, which calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)`. The runner itself is created at lines 161–171.

h01.
s3presign.Runner — every 12 hours — server/server.go:129

The `s3presign.Runner` in `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` re-presigns S3 attachment URLs so stored references stay valid (presigned URLs expire after 5 days; it refreshes ones that would lapse within 4 days). `runnerInterval` is `12 * time.Hour`. `Server.Start` hooks it in via `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` at `server/server.go:129`, which constructs the runner, runs it once, then starts `Run` on a 12-hour ticker.

value.text: The delivery function is `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It is protected by `safeDialContext` and `ValidateURL`, which check for reserved internal IP addresses.

Outbound HTTP delivery executes in the `Post` function at `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, via `safeClient.Do(req)`.

`PostAsync` merely queues work that later invokes `Post`. SSRF protection runs at dial time through `safeDialContext` and `safeClient` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. URL validation that rejects reserved and private IPs lives in `internal/webhook/validate.go` under `ValidateURL`, `isReservedIP`, and `reservedCIDRs`.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` is the runtime guard that blocks internal address delivery and also defeats DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` enforces restrictions only during URL creation or updates.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` is the runtime guard that blocks internal address delivery. It also defeats DNS rebinding, which `ValidateURL` cannot prevent. The reserved IP lists in `internal/webhook/validate.go` feed into that dial-time check.

h02.
Post — internal/webhook/webhook.go; safeDialContext (reserved/private IP block via isReservedIP) — internal/webhook/webhook.go

Outbound HTTP delivery runs in `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` (`safeClient.Do`). `PostAsync` only queues work; workers still call `Post`. Connections go through `safeDialContext` in the same file, which resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs using `isReservedIP` / `reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, IPv6 ULA). That dial-time check is the SSRF guard, including against DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` applies the same private-IP rule when a webhook URL is configured.

value.description: Parse internal function declarations with perl

value.text:
Over 269 declarations exist under internal/. I am tallying inbound calls for each to find the highest fan-in.

The main suspects are util.ConvertStringToInt32, util.HasPrefixes, and version.IsVersionGreaterThan. A Perl script will tally inbound calls, but whether to count same-name methods across types separately or together is still undecided.

I will count each declaration as distinct. Callers for same-name methods across types are hard to attribute because of interface dispatch. I will tally same-package and cross-package calls, then disambiguate common names. I will exclude the declaration itself and may exclude recursive calls. I will also count test files.

I will begin by grepping for exported functions, since they are more likely to have high cross-package fan-in. Unexported filter internals may have high intra-package fan-in instead.

value.description: Count inbound call sites for each internal function

value.text:
Method-name matching is polluted by false positives. `version.Len` catches generic `.Len()` calls from protobuf or standard library types. `scheduler.Next` may match unrelated `Next` methods from iterators or SQL packages.

A more careful approach is needed. Unique function names are more reliable than method names for counting callers. Common method names like Next, Len, and Parse require manual inspection of call sites. Exported unique functions are the real candidates. pkg.GenUUID shows 28 total calls. filter.addArg shows 28 same-package calls.

filter.Field and ast.Kind are too common to be reliable. renderer.renderChildren has 14 real callers. filter.jsonArrayExpr and filter.getConstValue each have 16 and 13 same-package calls. ConvertStringToInt32 may have been missed.

Package-level utility functions are being prioritized for accurate caller counts. version.IsVersionGreaterThan may have significant migration usage. The analysis will focus on non-method functions and uncommon method names.

Counting inbound callers for CompileToStatement. Many appear in tests. Need to check store, db, sqlite, and memo.go too.

CompileToStatement shows roughly 38 inbound callers across production and test files. addArg has 28 call sites plus its declaration. Still checking whether memo.go drivers call Compile directly or use CompileToStatement.

GenUUID has roughly 28 total callers. NewEngine has about 32. NewSchema has about 29. If test callers are excluded, addArg leads at 28 production callers, followed by jsonArrayExpr at 16 and renderChildren at 13.

getConstValue has roughly 13 inbound callers. I am now searching for additional high-fan-in symbols that may have been missed, such as isValidTagRune, qualifyColumn, and filter.Compile. I also need to verify whether memo.go drivers call Compile directly or exclusively use CompileToStatement.

DefaultEngine appears seven times in production. I am also checking store files for additional Compile and CompileToStatement usages.

User is the top persistent entity type by external package references. Memo ranks second. Proto store types may also qualify as persistent entities since they represent serialized forms.

Proto store types are defined in proto files rather than the data layer itself, so they likely do not count as persistent entities. User appears to be referenced by roughly 7 packages, while Memo is referenced by roughly 6. Excluding test packages would yield about 6 and 4 respectively.

Test packages are counted as external references. cmd does not directly reference either entity. The answer is ready.

h11.
1st: User (~7 packages); 2nd: Memo (~6 packages)

Persistent entities are the `store` structs (`Memo`, `User`, `Attachment`, and so on). Counting `store.Type` mentions outside `store/` and `proto/gen`, **User** shows up in seven packages: `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`. **Memo** is next with six: `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`. Dropping `_test.go` files still ranks User first (~6) then Memo (~4). Attachment is third (~3–4).

value.text:
The default driver is SQLite. Viper sets it via `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` and the flag defaults to `"sqlite"` in `cmd/memos/main.go`. The factory method `NewDBDriver` routes to `sqlite.NewDB` based on `profile.Driver`.

`Store.CreateMemo` delegates to `s.driver.CreateMemo`. The concrete INSERT is executed by `sqlite.DB.CreateMemo` in `store/db/sqlite/memo.go` at line 16. The SQL statement is at line 41. The determination method follows the default flag and viper setup through the factory switch to the SQLite implementation.

h12.
sqlite.DB.CreateMemo — store/db/sqlite/memo.go; default driver is sqlite via cmd/memos/main.go, selected by NewDBDriver

With no DB flags, `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` and the `--driver` default in `cmd/memos/main.go:122` / `:130` set `profile.Driver` to `"sqlite"`. `db.NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:18-20`) then constructs `sqlite.NewDB`. `store.Store.CreateMemo` only forwards to `s.driver.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109-113`). The INSERT that actually runs is `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` (`store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16-51`, `INSERT INTO \`memo\`` at line 41). MySQL and Postgres have the same method, but the factory never picks them on a default install.

Visibility is not only in `GetMemo`. Single-memo API reads go through `checkMemoReadAccess`; list/related-memo queries add `VisibilityList` / CEL `visibility` filters. Linked attachments are gated again on the API (`checkAttachmentAccess`) and on `/file` (`checkAttachmentPermission`). RSS and the sitemap only load `store.Public` memos. Live SSE delivery uses `canReceive` (private events only to the creator/admin). Outbound email uses `canViewerAccessMemo`. value.text: No Redis is configured. The cache layer uses in-process memory. User entries expire after 10 minutes via DefaultTTL. This is set during cache.Config construction and userCache.Set.

r01.
There is no Redis cache connection. Caching is an in-process memory `store/cache.Cache`; user entries use a 10-minute default TTL.

Nothing in the repo configures Redis (no client, DSN, or cache-backend flag). `store.New` in `store/store.go` builds `cache.Config{DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute, ...}` and `userCache: cache.New(cacheConfig)`. `store.Cache` is documented as a thread-safe in-memory cache (`store/cache/cache.go`). User writes go through `userCache.Set`, which applies `DefaultTTL` (`cache.go:92-94`). There is no user-specific TTL override.

value.text:
There is no nightly database-cleanup job. The scheduler package includes a daily-cleanup example at 2 AM in its documentation, but it is never constructed or registered in production.

The only background runner is s3presign, which runs every 12 hours.

r03.
There is no nightly database-cleanup cron job, so no scheduled time.

`internal/scheduler` is a reusable cron library. Its package docs (`internal/scheduler/doc.go`) only show a sample `"daily-cleanup"` at `"0 2 * * *"` (2 AM). Production never calls `scheduler.New` or `Register`. `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go`) starts only the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker, not a DB cleanup job. Cache “cleanup” is expired-entry eviction every 5 minutes (`store/store.go`, `store/cache/cache.go`), not a nightly database sweep.

value.text: There is no GraphQL schema. The public API is defined by protobuf files for gRPC services with Connect and gRPC-Gateway. An HTTP file server and RSS endpoints are also part of the API surface.

r05.
There is no GraphQL schema. The public API is protobuf RPC (Connect + gRPC-Gateway).

Services are defined under `proto/api/v1/` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, and the rest). `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` mounts gRPC-Gateway and Connect handlers at `/memos.api.v1.*`. Extra HTTP surfaces are the file server (`/file/...`), RSS, and the frontend—not GraphQL.
